# Chance Krenzer, Engineering Portfolio

> Chance Krenzer is a dual B.S. Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering student at Case Western Reserve University (Class of 2029). He designs, analyzes and flight-tests UAV hardware, from CAD and FEA through machining, printing and flight-log analysis. He is looking for a Summer 2027 internship or a Spring 2027 co-op.

Each project page separates model results from measurements and states what is still unproven.

## Projects

- [High-Speed Quadcopter](https://chancekrenzer.com/quadcopter/): CWRU design team, mechanical design lead, Dec 2025 to present. A 3D-printed quadcopter (16 printed airframe parts) designed for a 500 km/h level pass. Covers packaging and arm iteration, electronics selection worked from first principles (prop RPM limit and pitch speed, tip Mach, Kv and Kt, why 12S, voltage sag, resistive loss), a 243-configuration powertrain trade study in MATLAB that predicts 567 km/h for the selected setup and overruled his first motor choice on risk margin, SolidWorks Flow Simulation CFD, a PA6-CF versus PETG shell FEA comparison, and ArduPilot flight-log analysis of a 12 Hz roll oscillation and a 157 Hz vibration on the 6S electronics test frame. Trade study code: https://github.com/ChanceKrenzer/HSD-Mission-Model
- [VTOL Payload and Landing Gear](https://chancekrenzer.com/vtol/): CWRU VTOL Team, mechanical team specialist, Aug 2025 to present; the team placed 3rd of 20 at the 2026 championship. A fail-safe permanent-magnet payload plate (20 magnets installed, 7 required) released by a servo, and a landing-gear redesign using waterjet-cut aluminum brackets bonded in an alignment jig, with no gear failures at the championship.
- [ESP32 Quadcopter](https://chancekrenzer.com/esp32-quadcopter/): personal project, Dec 2025 to Feb 2026. Built from scratch for about $60: SolidWorks frame, hand-soldered MOSFET motor driver, ESP-NOW telemetry link, PID attitude control tuned on a 3-DOF gimbal, and measured 2:1 thrust-to-weight after tracing a voltage-sag problem to battery C-rating.
- [EMG Robotic Hand](https://chancekrenzer.com/emg-hand/): CWRU Hackathon, Nov 2025, 4th of 12 teams. A tendon-driven robotic hand that opens and closes on a MyoWare muscle signal over ESP-NOW, built in two days.
- [Making the Parts](https://chancekrenzer.com/shop/): shop work behind the projects. A steel hammer turned, milled and tapped from stock to ±0.010 in.; waterjet-cut aluminum brackets finished on the mill; jig bonding, heat-set inserts, thermoforming and FDM printing.

## Tools

SolidWorks (Certified SolidWorks Associate), PDM, GD&T drawings; SolidWorks Simulation and Flow Simulation; MATLAB; ArduPilot log analysis; Python, C/C++ (Arduino, ESP32), Java; CNC waterjet, manual mill and lathe, FDM printing, thermoforming, jig bonding.
